rubric.evidence: Every signature and behavior claim traces to a fetched primary source (all 2026-08-09): IDL quoted verbatim from the Blink module (spell_check_custom_dictionary.idl + document_spell_check_custom_dictionary.idl) and cross-checked against the explainer's identical IDL; validation rules (empty/whitespace/ill-formed-UTF-16, and why removeWords differs) read from spell_check_custom_dictionary.cc including its comments; caps (20000 words / 128 UTF-8 bytes) and the exact console-warning string from spellcheck_provider.cc + spellcheck_common.h; suppression semantics from spellcheck.cc; flag status from runtime_enabled_features.json5 at trunk AND branch-heads/7978; no dedicated chrome://flags entry verified against about_flags.cc (zero matches). The spec-PR naming divergence (window.spellCheckDictionary vs shipped document.spellCheckCustomDictionary) was verified from the PR diff and the published HTML Standard (contains neither) and is disclosed in the warn-block rather than papered over.

Feature id 6185007701557248 confirmed present in the milestone=153 listing under category 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)' (fetched 2026-08-09); listing name 'Spell Check Custom Dictionary API' slugs to spell-check-custom-dictionary-api per the repo rules; H1 uses the listing name; eyebrow says 'v153 · dev trial'.

reference-contract.json declares 5 inventory items (interface, Document attribute, addWords, removeWords, per-document word-set algorithm) x 9 dimensions; addWords and removeWords have dedicated child routes because their validation and refresh contracts genuinely differ; the only not-applicable is the readonly attribute's inputs, with a sourced rationale. Claimed implementation-sufficient for the SHIPPED dev-trial surface; the unsettled standards-level accessor name is disclosed prominently instead of being resolved by guesswork.

Lede states write-only design and purpose up front; warn-block gives exact enable steps (both flag routes), secure-context and spell-checking-on preconditions, and the naming-divergence caveat; the suppression model, availability matrix, and validation/limits each get their own scannable section; add-vs-remove refresh asymmetry is explained with its privacy rationale on the removeWords page.

Overview: feature-detect + basic addWords, plus an SPA view-scoping pattern with a cleanup closure. addWords page: explainer-derived vocabulary example and a runtime-fetched ticker-list example showing the cross-API sharing pattern. removeWords page: retraction and view-lifecycle examples. All semantic pre>code. No live showcase iframe: the CPS route returned 404 at build time (2026-08-09), honestly stated with Chromium's manual test page linked as the runnable alternative.

No BCD entry (api/SpellCheckCustomDictionary.json 404; no Document.json key) and zero webstatus.dev matches, both verified 2026-08-09 and linked; compat tables labelled interim and compiled from the milestone listing, flag status, and both vendor-position issues (Mozilla under consideration, WebKit no signal). Fallback guidance: feature-detect with 'in document', progressive enhancement, absent-feature cost is only red squiggles (cited to the ChromeStatus interop-risk field).

Zero unlinked source labels: every named artifact links directly (Blink IDL x2, module .cc, provider .cc, spellcheck.cc, spellcheck_common.h, runtime flags at trunk + M153 branch, about_flags.cc, Gerrit CL 7837649, both wpt_internal tests incl. a source.chromium.org mirror, whatwg PR, published HTML Standard section, explainer, TAG review, both standards positions, intent thread msgid link, tracking bug, webstatus query, BCD repo). The docs.google.com per-document-design doc on the ChromeStatus record was deliberately NOT linked (access-restricted Google doc); its claims are covered by the explainer and ChromeStatus record instead. All external links use target=_blank rel=noopener.

Single h1 per page, sequential h2 outline (route-card h3s nested under an h2); data tables use thead/th with scope semantics inherited from the shared house pattern; baseline banner uses role=note with aria-label; code examples are real text; color pairs come exclusively from public/styles.css variables (WCAG AA per repo invariant #5).

Long tokens (document.spellCheckCustomDictionary, --enable-blink-features=...) wrapped via overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1/lede/inline code; all tables inside .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} with min-width + table-layout:fixed; pre blocks scroll internally; verified via 1280px full-page screenshot and DOM dump against the local server (see writer report); no fixed widths beyond min-width guards.

The CPS feature route https://chrome-platform-showcase.paulkinlan-ea.deno.net/v153/spell-check-custom-dictionary-api/ returned HTTP 404 at build time (2026-08-09), so no iframe is embedded; the page links the future route in see-also and offers Chromium's add-remove-words-manual.html as the interactive stand-in. Upgrade to the standard embed when the demo ships.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables code blocks avoid horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on the browser layout engine and intrinsic sizing; use flex-wrap where overflow is possible; keep overflow contained in its own scroll container instead of hardcoding dimensions or letting the page scroll horizontally.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every data table renders inside .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} with table-layout:fixed and overflow-wrap:anywhere on cells; pre blocks scroll internally; .baseline-browsers uses flex-wrap; the only fixed dimensions are min-width guards; long code tokens wrap via overflow-wrap:anywhere.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible warning callout note banner semantics screen reader
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Structure content with landmarks and a sequential heading outline; use semantic tables with proper th scoping; don't fake headings; give supplementary banners appropriate note semantics rather than div soup.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: baseline banner is role=note with aria-label; warn-blocks lead with a visually and programmatically distinct strong label inside the flow; h1-h2 outline is sequential on all three pages; compat/validation tables use thead + th; examples are text, not images.

openQuestions: Will the shipped accessor stay document.spellCheckCustomDictionary, or move to window.spellCheckDictionary as the open whatwg/html#12590 PR proposes? The pages document the dev-trial surface and flag the divergence; re-verify when the PR merges or the intent-to-ship lands.

The Blink runtime feature is 'experimental' with no dedicated chrome://flags entry (verified trunk + branch-heads/7978, 2026-08-09); if the feature graduates to an origin trial or gains its own flag entry, the warn-block enable steps need updating.
Do the 20000-word / 128-byte caps become standardized? The explainer leaves limits implementation-defined and flags revisiting them for interop; the whatwg PR does not specify them.

The ChromeStatus record's per-document-design details live in an access-restricted Google doc (deliberately not linked); if Igalia publishes the design notes publicly, link them from the security section.

followUpGoals.goal: Re-verify the accessor name and spec status when whatwg/html#12590 merges or an intent-to-ship is sent: update the syntax section, warn-block, and reference-contract inventory if the surface renames to window.spellCheckDictionary (targeted fix, keep the route).

Re-check SpellCheckCustomDictionaryAPI's runtime status each milestone; when it leaves 'experimental' (origin trial or enabled-by-default), rewrite the enable steps, Baseline banner, and compatibility rows accordingly.
When the Chrome Platform Showcase ships v153/spell-check-custom-dictionary-api/, replace the text fallback in the examples section with the standard live iframe embed.
If BCD gains api.SpellCheckCustomDictionary (or the renamed surface) or webstatus.dev registers the feature, rebuild the interim compatibility tables from the canonical data on all three routes.
